content_of_post_to_comment: We have an epidemic of unread writers almost entirely educated in storytelling by cinema, video games, and role-playing games. So, when they decide to write a story, they end up transcribing a story that would better fit a visual medium. This leaves them blind to the many unique strengths of fictional literature.
comment: The interesting tension is that cinema trains writers to think in images, but literature’s power often lies in what cannot be shown. Perhaps the challenge isn’t escaping visual influence, but learning where to let imagination do the work.
